text:
Artem Duda is a rookie defenseman, a second-round pick by the franchise in 2022 (then the Coyotes) out of CSKA's system, who has played six NHL games since late October as the Mammoth's blue line thinned. He has no points yet and seven shots, playing almost 15 minutes a night.

Six games is too few to judge, but the early signs are reasonable. Utah takes 56% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about the team rate, and the Mammoth have scored 5.6 fewer goals than the chances deserve during his shifts. That's bad luck, and it's why he doesn't have a point. His AHL season in Tucson last year, 13 points in 27 games, translates to roughly 19 points over 82 NHL games.

History is a sober guide. Of the 112 defensemen picked 26th to 46th since 2005 who've had four or more seasons, 39 reached 200 NHL games, and the median first full season was 0.21 points a game. Our talent range, wide because the sample is tiny, has him somewhere between 5 and 22 points. Watch whether he keeps a spot once Nate Schmidt is back.
